record.paper_title: SOFT PHYSICS AND INTERMITTENCY : OPEN QUESTION(S) in KRAKOW
record.original_question: If Bose-Einstein correlations in multiparticle production are scale invariant, what space-time source structure produces them: event-by-event smooth sources with singular fluctuations between events, fractal sources whose own dynamics are scale invariant, or another mechanism distinguishable through higher-order Bose-Einstein correlations involving more than two particles?

evidence.quote: If confirmed by a detailed analysis of these very near-by correlations, this would mean a scale-invariant behaviour of the Bose-Einstein mechanism itself.

Now, two cases, at least, are possible: the source is event-by-event smooth (not fractal), but it fluctuates with a singular distribution from event to event; Or, a source is not characterized by a smooth curve , but is itself a fractal object in space-time, and the scale-invariant behaviour is then a consequence of the scale-invariant structure of the dynamics (as in classical intermittency).

One problem on previous studies raised by this approach is the lack of solid derivation of the Bose-Einstein correlations when there exist correlated sources, since the Hanbury-Twiss phenomenon is for uncorrelated sources. A key phenomenological conclusion of this work is the necessity to look for higher-order Bose-Einstein correlations (with more than 2 particles involved) as a way of distinguishing the various mechanisms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In high-energy multiparticle production, two-particle Bose-Einstein correlations are commonly described by a correlation function C_2(q) that depends on the relative four-momentum q of two identical bosons. Suppose that empirically C_2(q) exhibits scale-invariant (power-law) behavior of the form C_2(q) - 1 ~ q^{- eta} as q -> 0, indicating a scale-invariant Bose-Einstein mechanism. Two candidate space-time pictures of the emitting source are proposed:

(a) the source is, on each event, a smooth (non-fractal) space-time emission region, but the parameters characterizing that smooth source fluctuate from event to event with a singular (broad, possibly Lévy-stable type) distribution, so that the observed scale invariance arises after averaging over events;

(b) the source itself is a fractal object in space-time, so that the scale-invariant two-particle correlation is a direct consequence of the scale-invariant (intermittent) dynamics of the source.

Determine which of these scenarios (or which alternative mechanism) generates the observed scale-invariant two-particle Bose-Einstein correlations. In particular: derive, in a setting allowing correlated emitting sources (going beyond the standard Hanbury Brown–Twiss assumption of fully uncorrelated sources), the predicted higher-order Bose-Einstein correlation functions C_n(q_1,...,q_{n-1}) for n >= 3 identical bosons in each of these scenarios, and identify observable features of these higher-order correlations that distinguish (a) from (b) and from any other mechanism producing the same scale-invariant C_2.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether scale-invariant Bose-Einstein correlations in multiparticle production arise from event-by-event fluctuating smooth sources, from intrinsically fractal space-time sources, or from another mechanism remains an active research topic. Subsequent work has explored Lévy-stable parametrizations, two-radii parametrizations and higher-order BEC measurements (e.g. at UA1, L3, ALICE), but no consensus derivation in the correlated-source case nor a definitive experimental discrimination via n>=3 BECs has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Lévy Distributions for One-Dimensional Analysis of the Bose–Einstein Correlations
status_evidence.snippet: Stable (Lévy) distributions are among the most promising tools for studying fractal-like space-time extent of emission regions; power-law parametrization C2(q)~q^-β serves as a signature for fractal-like sources.
status_evidence.claim: Fractal/Lévy source descriptions of BEC remain under active investigation, indicating the discrimination problem is not closed.

status_evidence.title: Two scales in Bose–Einstein correlations
status_evidence.snippet: Bose-Einstein correlations of two emitted identical particles should be described by a 'two-radii' parametrization arising from small-size sources distributed over a larger impact-parameter region.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work still proposes new source structures to explain BEC, showing the underlying source-structure question remains debated.

status_evidence.title: Higher Order Bose-Einstein Correlation Functions of Identical Particles
status_evidence.snippet: A diagram technique has been formulated to calculate higher order Bose-Einstein correlations.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-order BEC formalism has been developed but is still being applied to distinguish source models.

status_evidence.title: Fractals 30 (2022) 2240039
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2022) work continues to study fractal/scaling features of multiparticle production.
status_evidence.claim: Fractal-source interpretations of multiparticle correlations are still being investigated as of 2022.
